findings.evidence: Both excision applications assert that the closure of the excised complement lies in the interior of the subspace, but the complement in 2.1 meets the outer boundary of D² and the complement in 3.1 meets the boundary of D²×[0,1]. The cited excision theorem requires closure inside int_X(A), so the claimed relative-homology reductions are not justified. Step 1.1 can give the punctured-disk homology directly; the string-link exterior calculation needs a boundary-compatible relative-homology proof or an authoritative source verifying the H₁/H₂ maps.
